title: Cohen coordinate completion of an equicharacteristic regular local ring
statement:
Let $(B,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian regular local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme], complete for $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose $B$ contains $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$. Put $F=B/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field] and $d=\dim B$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. There are a ring section $\sigma:F\to B$ of the residue map and elements $t_1,\ldots,t_d\in\mathfrak m$ such that the continuous map
$$F[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]\xrightarrow{\sim}B,\qquad a\longmapsto\sigma(a),\quad T_i\longmapsto t_i,$$
is an isomorphism, where formal power series have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. In particular $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ generate $\mathfrak m$. For $C=F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $I=(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$, the map $C\to B$ above induces an isomorphism $\widehat C_I\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ from the $I$-adic completion, preserving the coordinate images and inducing the identity on the quotients $C/I=F=B/\mathfrak m$. This includes $d=0$, with the empty coordinate tuple and $C=F$.

source.place: Tag 0C0S, lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field, clauses (1) and (2) and proof (Cohen coefficient field and parameters of length dim B); the final coordinate-completion formulation is the coefficientwise description of the I-adic completion of F[T_1,...,T_d].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] to the complete local ring $B$. It gives a subring $\Lambda\subset B$ with maximal ideal $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m=p\Lambda$ and residue isomorphism $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\cong F$, where $p=\operatorname{char}F$. If $\mathbf Q\subset B$, each nonzero integer is a unit in $B$, so remains nonzero in $F$; thus $p=0$. If $\mathbf F_p\subset B$, then $pB=0$, hence also $p\Lambda=0$. In either case the maximal ideal of $\Lambda$ is zero, so $\Lambda$ is a field and its residue map $\Lambda\to F$ is an isomorphism. Define $\sigma:F\to B$ as its inverse followed by inclusion. Its composite with $B\to F$ is the identity.

The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated by Noetherianity [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The dimension bound [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators] makes $d=\dim B$ a finite nonnegative integer (the maximal ideal gives a prime). By the definition of regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], choose $d$ generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathfrak m$. They belong to $\mathfrak m$. This uses no prescribed coefficient embedding or smoothness of $F$ over a chosen subfield.

source.place: Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local; Tag 0C0S, proof of (2), choice of parameters

proof.text: Put $P=F[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$ and $J=(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with coefficient field $F$, $P$ is a Noetherian complete local domain, its maximal ideal is $J$, its residue field is $F$, and $\dim P=d$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to the $\mathfrak m$-adically complete ring $B$, the map $\sigma$, and the elements $t_i\in\mathfrak m$. Obtain $\Phi:P\to B$ with $\Phi(T_i)=t_i$ and $\Phi|_F=\sigma$. Its formula modulo $\mathfrak m^n$ is evaluation of the terms of degree $<n$. Since the $t_i$ generate $\mathfrak m$, $JB=\mathfrak m$. The map $P\to B/JB=F$ is surjective already on constants. The source is $J$-adically complete and the target is $JB$-adically Hausdorff; thus [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] gives surjectivity of $\Phi$.

source.place: Tag 0C0S, lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field, proof of (2), continuous map and surjectivity; Tag 0315, lemma-completion-generalities, (1)

proof.text: The kernel is zero. Indeed, if $0\ne f\in\ker\Phi$, choose a chain of prime ideals $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_d$ in $B$. Such a chain exists because $\dim B=d$ is finite: the bounded set of possible integral chain lengths attains its supremum [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Inverse images under the surjective $\Phi$ are a strict chain of primes in $P$, all containing $f$. Since $P$ is a domain [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $(0)$ is a prime strictly below the first inverse image. Prepending it gives a chain of length $d+1$ in $P$, contradicting $\dim P=d$. Thus $\Phi$ is a ring isomorphism. As $\Phi(J)=\mathfrak m$, it and its inverse preserve all powers of the respective maximal ideals, hence are continuous.

source.place: Tag 0C0S, lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field, last sentence; prime-chain proof of the dimension-drop argument

proof.text: Set $C=F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$, $I=(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$. From the monomial description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I^n$ consists exactly of the polynomials whose monomials all have total degree $\ge n$: a monomial of degree $\ge n$ factors by one of degree $n$, and conversely every product of $n$ variables has degree $n$. Thus a class in $C/I^n$ has a unique representative supported in degrees $<n$. In a compatible sequence of such classes [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], the coefficient of $T^E$ is constant once $n>|E|$. Assigning these stable coefficients gives a map $\theta:\widehat C_I\to P$; the inverse sends $\sum_Ea_ET^E$ to $(\sum_{|E|<n}a_ET^E\bmod I^n)_n$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. There are finitely many monomials of each bounded degree because $d$ is finite. These formulas are inverse; they preserve addition coefficientwise and multiplication because the coefficient of $T^G$ is the finite sum $\sum_{E+H=G}a_Eb_H$. Consequently $\theta$ is an $F$-algebra isomorphism sending each coordinate to the same coordinate. The required map is $\Phi\theta$. For each $n$, its residue in $B/\mathfrak m^n$ is evaluation of the representative of the $n$th class at the $t_i$, by the evaluation formula in step 3. It is therefore the map on completions induced by $C\to B$, not merely an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Section Tag 00M9, section-completion, and Definition Tag 0317, definition-complete; elementary coefficientwise construction extending Tag 0C0S

proof.text: Modulo $I$, $\theta$ sends a class to its constant coefficient, and $\Phi$ then sends $a\in F$ to $\sigma(a)$, whose residue is $a$. Hence the induced map $C/I=F\to B/\mathfrak m=F$ is the identity. If $d=0$, regularity made $\mathfrak m$ generated by the empty tuple, so $\mathfrak m=0$ and $F=B$. The ring $P$ in zero variables is $F$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], while $C=F$ and $I=0$; the inverse limit defining its completion is the constant system $F$, so $\widehat C_0=F$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. All maps above reduce to $\sigma:F\cong B$, with no variables or positive-dimension assumption.
